title: Enicepatide (CT-388): Roche's Dual GLP-1/GIP Agonist With 22.5% Weight Loss in Phase 2 — Research Dossier
excerpt: Enicepatide (CT-388, RO7795068) is Roche and Genentech's once-weekly dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist. Phase 2 obesity data show 22.5% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 48 weeks — matching the best-in-class benchmarks — while a September 2026 Phase 2 diabetes trial reported a 2.65% HbA1c reduction. Phase 3 ENITH trials are now underway.
content:
What Is Enicepatide?

Enicepatide (research codes: CT-388, RO7795068) is a once-weekly injectable dual GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist developed by Roche and its US subsidiary Genentech. It simultaneously activates both the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR) — the same two receptors engaged by tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound), but via Roche's proprietary molecular scaffold rather than Lilly's.

Enicepatide has completed two Phase 2 trials with compelling efficacy data, and in 2026 Roche initiated the Phase 3 ENITH program with two obesity trials. The drug is also being investigated in combination with petrelintide (Roche/Genentech's amylin analog) based on preliminary data suggesting additive weight-loss effects from complementary satiety mechanisms.

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

Mechanism of Action

Enicepatide co-activates two incretin receptors:

  • GLP-1 receptor: reduces appetite via hypothalamic and brainstem signaling, slows gastric emptying, stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion
  • GIP receptor: augments insulin secretion, may improve adipose tissue insulin sensitivity, and in combination with GLP-1R activation appears to amplify weight loss beyond what either receptor alone achieves — a synergy first clinically validated by tirzepatide

Roche built enicepatide on a distinct molecular platform, potentially offering different tolerability or tissue-distribution characteristics compared to tirzepatide's fatty-acid-conjugated design.

Key Research Findings

Phase 2 Obesity Trial — CT-388-103 (N=469, 48 Weeks)

  • Population: adults with obesity or overweight without type 2 diabetes
  • Results at 24 mg (highest dose):
    • Placebo-adjusted mean body weight reduction: −22.5% (efficacy estimand — treats discontinuations as if drug continued)
    • Treatment-regimen estimand: −18.3% (includes discontinuations)
    • Weight loss curve had not plateaued at week 48, suggesting continued potential with longer treatment
  • Safety: consistent with GLP-1/GIP RA class; discontinuation rate due to AEs was low

Phase 2 Type 2 Diabetes Trial — CT-388-104 (N=447, 48 Weeks, Topline September 22, 2026)

  • Population: adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity; baseline HbA1c 8.1%
  • Results at 24 mg:
    • Body weight reduction: approximately −15.5%
    • HbA1c reduction: −2.65 percentage points from baseline — a clinically meaningful glycemic improvement
  • Safety: discontinuation due to adverse events 2.0% enicepatide vs. 0.0% placebo; no new safety signals

Phase 3 ENITH Program (Initiated 2026)

  • Two Phase 3 obesity trials initiated in 2026
  • Full registration details and primary completion dates expected at a major 2027 medical conference
  • Combination strategy with petrelintide (amylin analog) in development — Roche announced plans for a combination trial as of late 2026

Dosing in Research

All dosing information reflects investigational research protocols only.

  • Once-weekly subcutaneous injection
  • Dose range explored in Phase 2: up to 24 mg weekly
  • Standard GLP-1 RA precautions apply; GIP co-agonism does not appear to add significant new safety concerns beyond the class

FAQ

How does enicepatide compare to tirzepatide (Mounjaro)?

Both are dual GLP-1/GIP agonists, but from different companies with different molecular scaffolds. Tirzepatide showed ~22.5% weight loss in SURMOUNT-1 at 72 weeks (15 mg). Enicepatide's Phase 2 (48 weeks, efficacy estimand) showed 22.5% placebo-adjusted weight loss. These are not directly comparable across different trial designs and durations. No head-to-head data exists. Tirzepatide is FDA-approved; enicepatide is in Phase 3.

What Phase 3 program is Roche running for enicepatide?

The program is called ENITH. Two Phase 3 obesity trials were initiated in 2026 following the strong Phase 2 data. Roche is also exploring a combination of enicepatide plus petrelintide (its amylin analog in Phase 3) to target complementary satiety pathways — GLP-1/GIP (incretin) plus amylin simultaneously. Full ENITH trial details are pending.

What were enicepatide's results in people with type 2 diabetes?

CT-388-104 Phase 2 (N=447, 48 weeks, topline September 22, 2026): 24 mg dose produced ~15.5% weight loss and a 2.65 percentage-point drop in HbA1c from a baseline of 8.1%. Discontinuation rate due to AEs: 2.0% vs. 0.0% placebo. Full peer-reviewed publication pending. Not approved for use in T2D or any indication. Consult a healthcare provider.

Research Limitations

  • Phase 2 data are topline/company-reported; full peer-reviewed publications not yet available for CT-388-103 or CT-388-104
  • The 22.5% efficacy-estimand figure and 18.3% treatment-regimen figure diverge substantially — the choice of estimand significantly affects interpretation
  • Cross-trial comparisons to tirzepatide are not statistically valid (different populations, durations, estimands)
  • Phase 3 ENITH trials not yet completed; regulatory approval not expected before 2028–2029
  • Long-term safety data and cardiovascular outcomes evidence not yet available

Disclaimer

Enicepatide (CT-388) is an investigational compound. This article is for educational and research purposes only. It is not medical advice and does not constitute a recommendation for use. Enicepatide is not approved by the FDA, EMA, or any other regulatory agency. Do not use investigational compounds outside of authorized clinical trials.
